game.name: Peglin
game.short_description: Peglin is a Pachinko Roguelike - Fight enemies by collecting special orbs and popping pegs to deal damage. Acquire special relics that radically change the game and ensure no two runs are the same. Aim carefully to survive in this unique turn-based RPG!

other_scores.score: Scores apply to the Nintendo Switch version only

commentary.label: Tier list Part 1 (2023)
commentary.summary: Peglin is a Peggle-style roguelike where you launch a ball at pegs and the result damages enemies. He calls it a great example of someone taking a unique idea and making it a roguelike. He has put hundreds of hours into it over several years and keeps returning as it gets regular updates. He places it in S tier, while saying it is not quite the masterpiece of the other S tier games.
praise: Every run feels very different thanks to varied builds, characters and relics
Many unique orbs and events keep fights fun and engaging
Strong blend of RNG and skill, with deserved broken runs now and then
Continuous updates add new characters and orbs roughly monthly
Good pacing, helped by an option to speed up the game
criticism: Gameplay looks a bit old or slow at first glance, though speed-up mitigates it
Not quite as masterful as the top S tier games
unique_points: Fuses Peggle-style ball physics with roguelike build-crafting
Player skill matters alongside RNG, unusual for a luck-based genre
commentary.quote: it has no right being this good it is an absolute s tier for me
design_criteria: Run variety: builds, characters, relics make each run distinct
Synergies and broken runs: rare overpowered runs feel earned
Skill vs RNG: a balanced blend
Content and support: frequent updates with new characters and orbs
Pacing: speed-up option keeps runs moving
Event and orb diversity: many unique options keep fights engaging

community.one_liner: A Peggle-style pachinko roguelite from Red Nexus Games where you launch orbs at pegs to damage enemies while collecting relics and upgrading orbs across a run.
community.consensus_summary: Peglin is well liked by players (Steam 'Very Positive', about 84% of roughly 17.7k reviews) and mixed-to-favorable among the few critics who covered it (Metacritic 76 from 8 reviews on Switch, user score 6.9 from 29 ratings). The core loop of bouncing orbs around a peg board and building synergies with relics is widely called addictive and great for short sessions, including on Steam Deck, Switch and mobile. The recurring complaints are heavy RNG, only three acts for most of the game's life, steep late-game (Cruciball) difficulty and repetition. It launched in Early Access in April 2022, hit 1.0 and Switch on Aug 27, 2024, and is still being updated; a 2.0 update in March 2026 reportedly added a fourth act, new items, enemies and music.
best_things: The Peggle-meets-Slay-the-Spire premise is fresh and the core loop of aiming, bouncing and watching damage numbers climb is described as satisfying and dopamine-heavy
Easy to learn and pick up; runs are short (one reviewer averages about 50 minutes) and the game can be saved and resumed, which suits casual or chill play
Build variety through orbs and relics; finding a combination that clicks and improvising around what you are offered is a common highlight
Multiple characters and the Cruciball difficulty ladder give replay value and let players choose between relaxed and punishing runs
Charming pixel art and music, and a developer team that keeps patching and is praised for listening to feedback
Works well on handheld and mobile (Steam Deck, Switch); Metacritic critics singled out the Switch version
Very high playtimes among fans (several reviewers report 250 to over 2,000 hours)
worst_things: Heavy RNG: orb trajectories are hard to control, so luck can outweigh skill, which critics and many negative Steam reviews cite
Limited content for a long stretch: only three acts plus a final boss, so runs feel samey and players can see everything quickly (the 2026 fourth act is meant to address this)
Uneven option balance: some relics and orbs are seen as near-useless while others are mandatory at higher difficulty
Cruciball levels add nerfs and tougher enemies rather than new mechanics, which some see as lazy difficulty scaling
Some enemy types and encounters (long-range damage you cannot avoid, the Wall boss, lines of exploding goblins) are cited as run-ending regardless of build
Unlocking characters and the true ending relies on grinding large counters such as debuffs applied or coins spent
Synergy traps: boss orbs with negative damage can silently break builds if you do not know how items interact
Price ($19.99) is questioned by some given the amount of content; many recommend buying on sale
improvements: More acts, areas, enemies, characters, orbs and relics; a recurring request even from positive reviewers
An endless or post-final-boss mode so players can keep testing builds and see new orbs without risking them early in a run
Let players choose map routes instead of having to shoot a ball and hope it lands on the desired path
Rework the late-game difficulty so it comes from interesting enemy design rather than stat nerfs and unavoidable damage
Better balance and clearer communication of item interactions and effect names for new players
Revisit the anti-save-scum behavior added in late Oct 2025 that, per a top negative review, counts quitting and resuming after a short session as save scumming and can ruin the run
unique_things: Pachinko/Peggle physics as the combat system in a turn-based roguelite, where you aim at enemies and pegs rather than play cards
Orbs act as the deck: you add and upgrade orbs, and relics modify how pegs and damage behave
Board layout and peg interaction matter more than a typical deckbuilder, yet the goal is damage accumulation rather than clearing the board like Peggle
Cruciball difficulty system for scaling challenge after winning
Began as a 48-hour game jam prototype ('Goblin Drop') and later won Best Design at the 2022 Taipei Game Show per Wikipedia
tedious_or_disliked: Grinding character unlocks and the true ending via large cumulative counters
Repetition of the same three biomes and similar boss encounters across many runs
Navigating the map by shooting a ball and hoping it lands on the path you want
Late-game frustration at Cruciball 5+, where reviewers report physics feeling erratic, refresh orbs in awkward spots, and enemies that counter common builds
Runs that go badly snowball with little chance to recover, which some find miserable
Anti-save-scum rule after Oct 2025 interfering with short stop-and-resume sessions
divisive_points: RNG: fans see it as part of the fun and improvisation, detractors see gambling-like luck that undermines build planning
Difficulty: patches are said by some to make the game easier while others say higher Cruciball levels are unfairly stacked
Value: some call it one of the best games for the price, others say it is only worth it on sale due to limited content
Whether it plays like Peggle: some love the nostalgia, others note it plays quite differently and do not get the Peggle feel
community.reception_notes: Early Access on PC began April 25, 2022; mobile followed April 11, 2023; 1.0 and the Nintendo Switch release came Aug 27, 2024 (Steam lists this date). Wikipedia says it sold about 400,000 copies in its first year in Early Access. Steam-revenue-calculator estimates about $14.9M gross and $4.4M net revenue, and SteamSpy-style data gives 500k to 1M owners; both are estimates, not audited. Version 2.0 (March 16, 2026) reportedly added a fourth act, items, enemies and music. Steam reviews from late 2025 include a controversy over anti-save-scum changes, and recent reviews remain mostly positive with ongoing developer support. Metacritic has few scores (8 critic, 29 user) so they are a weak signal. Steam lists Windows and Mac only; Switch and mobile exist separately. No OpenCritic listing could be confirmed; the web search budget was exhausted, so Reddit and outlet reviews could not be fetched (Reddit fetch was blocked).
